stem: During a transfer request, an Ativan prescription from a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner was issued 20 days ago and is verified. What is the key Massachusetts determination?

choices.text: Reject it after five days under the out-of-state Schedule II narcotic rule if its alternate trigger can be documented.
The out-of-state Schedule IV prescription may be filled within 30 days after required verification.
Use the federal six-month clock as the only deadline.
Accept it without verification because Connecticut licenses the practitioner.
Require a Massachusetts prescriber for every Schedule IV prescription.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'The out-of-state Schedule IV prescription may be filled within 30 days after required verification.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Reject it after five days under the out-of-state Schedule II narcotic rule.' would require that lorazepam were a Schedule II narcotic. The decisive cue appears in 'During a transfer request, an Ativan prescription from a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner was issued 20 days ago and is verified. What is the key Massachusetts determination?'.

What is the key Massachusetts determination?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'The out-of-state Schedule IV prescription may be filled within 30 days after required verification.': supported by out-of-state iii-vi.
choice_analysis.C: 'Use the federal six-month clock as the only deadline.' would apply only if federal refill timing displaced Massachusetts' 30-day initial-fill condition; 'During a transfer request, an Ativan prescription from a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner was issued 20 days ago and is verified. What is the key Massachusetts determination?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Accept it without verification because Connecticut licenses the practitioner.' would apply only if Massachusetts did not require verification for out-of-state Schedule III-V prescriptions; 'During a transfer request, an Ativan prescription from a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner was issued 20 days ago and is verified. What is the key Massachusetts determination?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Require a Massachusetts prescriber for every Schedule IV prescription.' would apply only if Massachusetts prohibited the statutory out-of-state pathway; 'During a transfer request, an Ativan prescription from a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner was issued 20 days ago and is verified. What is the key Massachusetts determination?' states otherwise.

related_facts: lorazepam (Ativan) is used for anxiety disorders and short-term relief of anxiety symptoms; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.

An authorized out-of-state practitioner may issue a Schedule III through VI prescription filled in Massachusetts within 30 days of issue; Schedule III through V prescriptions require pharmacist verification.
